headline: Satellite Internet Applicant Decides To Just Build His Own Low-Earth Orbit Constellation After Waiting In Line At DoT Office For Six Months
body:
Aakash Gupta, a software engineer from Bengaluru, has announced he is abandoning his application for a satellite broadband license in favor of launching 400 custom-built micro-satellites from his balcony after his DoT file remained stuck in a ‘Pending – Beverage Refill In Progress’ state since March.

“The bureaucrats were very polite, but every time I asked about my status, they handed me a token that literally just says ‘Tomorrow’ in calligraphy,” said Gupta, who has repurposed his kitchen into a miniature clean-room facility. “I realized that by the time they finish checking the structural integrity of my hypothetical space-beam infrastructure, I could have already engineered, launched, and phased out a two-generation satellite network using spare motherboard parts and a high-altitude weather balloon.”

Department officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, maintained that no bias exists in the current queueing system, noting that Gupta’s application is currently resting comfortably between a proposal to establish an underwater carrier pigeon network and a request to beam internet directly through cosmic rays. “We treat all applicants with equal levels of profound, indeterminate stagnation,” the official noted while stamping a document with a ‘Processing Pending Approval Pending’ seal.
caption: When the government asks you to wait for a satellite license, you decide to just become a space tycoon. It’s called efficiency. 🛰️🚀 #SpaceTech #Startups #Bureaucracy #IndianTech (satire)
igHook: Tag someone whose patience for bureaucracy is officially lower than a low-earth orbit satellite.
imagePrompt: A cluttered apartment balcony filled with complex electronics, loose circuit boards, and a large, amateur-looking satellite dish pointed toward a clear blue sky.

sourceHeadline.title: DoT refutes bias in Starlink authorisation, says all licensees’ approvals pending

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 is the clear winner because it offers a distinct, high-energy escalation of the premise (building a personal satellite constellation) rather than relying on the tired 'waiting for a bureaucratic response' trope. It uses vivid, specific invented details like the 'Tomorrow' calligraphy token and the kitchen-based clean room, maintaining a punchy, deadpan tone throughout.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictional persona to satirize bureaucratic delays. The narrative is clearly absurd and hyperbolic, avoiding any real individuals, sensitive communal topics, or reputational damage to specific entities.
